## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThetoString()method returns the string itself.

This method may seem redundant, but its purpose is to allow code that is treating the string as a more generalized object to know its string value without casting it toStringtype.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return a string's value:
String myStr = "Hello, World!";
System.out.println(myStr.toString());
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThetoUpperCase()method converts a string to upper case letters.

Note:ThetoLowerCase()method converts a string to lower case letters.

None.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Convert a string to upper case and lower case letters:
String txt = "Hello World";
System.out.println(txt.toUpperCase());
System.out.println(txt.toLowerCase());
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

Thetrim()method removes whitespace from both ends of a string.

Note:This method does not change the original string.

None.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Remove whitespace from both sides of a string:
String myStr = "       Hello World!       ";
System.out.println(myStr);
System.out.println(myStr.trim());
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThevalueOf()method returns the string representation of the specified value.

One of the following:

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return a string representation of different data types:
char[] myArray = {'a', 'b', 'c'};
System.out.println(String.valueOf(myArray));
System.out.println(String.valueOf('A'));
System.out.println(String.valueOf(true));
System.out.println(String.valueOf(4.5f));
System.out.println(String.valueOf(5.2));
System.out.println(String.valueOf(12));
System.out.println(String.valueOf(1400L));
Try it Yourself »
```
